Rashi on Pesachim 109a:1:1.english: Roasted grains - Parched grain from old wheat.

Rashi on Pesachim 109a:1:2.hebrew: חוטפין מצה - מגביהין את הקערה בשביל תינוקות שישאלו. ואית דמפרש: חוטפין מצה — אוכלין מהר. וזה הלשון עיקר, מדמייתי הא דר"ע בהדה:
Rashi on Pesachim 109a:1:2.english: One grabs matzah - They lift up the [Seder] platter on account of the children, so that they will ask. And there are those who explain: "One grabs matzah" [means] eating quickly. And this wording is the primary [explanation], since [the Gemara] cites this [statement] of Rabbi Akiva alongside it.

Rashi on Pesachim 109a:2:1.english: Except for the eves of Passover - So that the children would sleep during the day, and not at night at the time of the Haggadah.

Rashi on Pesachim 109a:6:1.english: A kista of muryas [fish brine] - A measure with which they sell the muryas.

Rashi on Pesachim 109a:6:2.english: The old eighth [measure] - A measure that was formerly in it, in Tiberias.

Rashi on Pesachim 109a:6:3.english: [It] was greater - than the current eighth [measure] [by] a quarter[-log].

Rashi on Pesachim 109a:6:4.hebrew: ובה משערין רביעית לפסח - שהיו ממלאין אותה ומנערין אותה לתוך אותה של עכשיו עד שהיא מליאה, ומים הנשארים בתמנתא הן הן רביעית:
Rashi on Pesachim 109a:6:4.english: And with it they measure a revi'it for Passover - For they would fill it and pour it into the current one until it is full, and the water remaining in the temanta [the old eighth-measure] is the revi'it.

Rashi on Pesachim 109a:7:1.english: By the height of two fingerbreadths - And by the height of half a fingerbreadth and the height of one-fifth of a fingerbreadth.

Rashi on Pesachim 109a:7:2.english: With large [fingerbreadths] - With the thumb, of which there are four fingerbreadths in a handbreadth.

Tosafot on Pesachim 109a:2:1.hebrew: חוץ מערבי פסחים - ה"ג רבינו שמואל, ולא נהירא: דאטו לא יוכלו לישן בלא אביהם? וטעם שני שפירש, שמא יעכבו עד שיחשך הרבה — אם כן לא היו צריכין לעמוד ביום כי אם בלילה! לכך נראה דגריס "לילי פסחים"; והיו רגילין בבית המדרש לילי י"ט, כדאמרינן (ביצה דף כא.): מעשה בשמעון התימני שלא בא בלילי י"ט לבית המדרש, למחר מצאו רבי יהודה בן בבא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 109a:2:1.english: Except for the eves of Passover - Rabbenu Shemuel reads [the text] thus, but it does not seem [correct], for could [the children] not sleep without their father? And [as for] the second reason that he explained — lest they delay [in the study hall] until it becomes very dark — if so, they would not have needed to arise during the day, but only at night! Therefore, it appears that [one should] read: "the nights of Passover"; for they were accustomed [to learn] in the study hall on the nights of a Festival, as we say (Beitzah 21a): An incident occurred with Shimon HaTimni, who did not come to the study hall on the night of a Festival; the next day, Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava found him:

Tosafot on Pesachim 109a:3:1.hebrew: שנאמר ושמחת אתה וביתך - תימה, דהאי קרא גבי מעשר שני כתיב בפ' ראה, ולא מייתי קרא דכתיב בפ' ראה גבי רגל: "ושמחת אתה ובנך ובתך"? וי"ל, דיליף ממעשר, דכתיב ביתו בהדיא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 109a:3:1.english: As it is stated: "And you shall rejoice, you and your household" - It is puzzling, for this verse is written regarding the second tithe in Parashat Re'eh, and [the Gemara] does not cite the verse that is written in Parashat Re'eh regarding the Festival: "And you shall rejoice, you and your son and your daughter"? And one can say that it derives [this] from [the verse about] tithe, where "his household" is written explicitly.

Tosafot on Pesachim 109a:3:2.hebrew: במה משמחו ביין - היינו בזמן הזה, אבל בזמן בית המקדש אין שמחה אלא בבשר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 109a:3:2.english: "With what does one make him rejoice? With wine" - This refers to the present time, but in the time of the Temple there is no rejoicing except with meat.

Tosafot on Pesachim 109a:4:1.hebrew: בא"י בכלי פשתן המגוהצין - אבל בבבל לא היו בקיאים לגהץ, כדאמר (תענית כט:): גיהוץ שלנו ככיבוס שלהם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 109a:4:1.english: In Eretz Yisrael, with pressed linen garments - But in Babylonia they were not skilled at pressing [clothes], as it says (Taanit 29b): "Our pressing is like their washing."

Tosafot on Pesachim 109a:5:1.hebrew: וזבחת שלמים ואכלת שם ושמחת - תימה, דהאי קרא בהר עיבל כתיב, ולא מייתי קרא דושמחת בחגך, דדרשינן מיניה בחגיגה (דף ח.): לרבות כל מיני שמחות לשמחה, מכאן אמרו ישראל יוצאין ידי חובתן בנדרים ונדבות. וי"ל, משום דהכא בהדיא כתיב "וזבחת שלמים ושמחת":
Tosafot on Pesachim 109a:5:1.english: "And you shall sacrifice peace-offerings and you shall eat there and you shall rejoice" - [This is] surprising, for this verse is written regarding Mount Ebal, and [the Gemara] does not cite the verse "And you shall rejoice on your festival" [Deuteronomy 16:14], from which we derive in Chagigah (8a) to include all types of rejoicing for [the mitzvah of] rejoicing; from here [the Sages] said [that] Israel fulfills their obligation with vowed and freewill offerings. And one can answer: because here it is explicitly written, "And you shall sacrifice peace-offerings ... and you shall rejoice."

Tosafot on Pesachim 109a:6:1.hebrew: תמניתא - פי' רשב"ם דהיינו תומן ועוכלא. ולא נהירא, דבהמוכר את הספינה (ב"ב דף צ.) חשיב: לוג, ורביעית הלוג, תומן, ועוכלא, וכל מדה ומדה פוחתת והולכת — וכאן משמע שהיא יותר מרביעית:
Tosafot on Pesachim 109a:6:1.english: Temanita [The eighth measure] - Rashbam explained that this is a toman and an ukhla. But this does not seem right, for in [the chapter] HaMokher Et HaSefinah (Bava Batra 90a) it lists: the log, the quarter-log, the toman, and the ukhla, and each measure is progressively smaller — whereas here it is implied that it is larger than a quarter-log.
